title: FreeLoc: Online Floorplan Localization via Diffusion-Aided Pose Refinement
title_zh: FreeLoc：基于扩散辅助姿态精化的在线平面图定位方法

paragraphs.en: Floorplans provide compact and widely available geometric maps for indoor localization, but existing high-performing floorplan-based methods still convert them into dense scene-specific offline databases, tying accuracy, storage, and runtime to the sampling resolution of the discretized pose space. We present FreeLoc, an online RGB-based floorplan localization framework that treats the floorplan as a directly queryable geometric map. FreeLoc introduces an efficient online geometric querying and diffusion-aided refinement scheme, which retrieves plausible pose anchors through on-the-fly floorplan ray querying and refines them into accurate continuous pose estimates. For sequential localization, FreeLoc develops an online likelihood construction strategy that bridges single-frame localization and probabilistic temporal fusion by constructing likelihoods from coarse-sampled candidates and refined pose hypotheses, enabling histogram-filter-based temporal fusion without offline databases. Experiments demonstrate real-time online inference and state-of-the-art performance in both single-frame and sequential localization, while real-world results validate practical deployability in indoor robotic localization scenarios.

paragraphs.en: Indoor camera localization is a core capability for robotic perception and embodied intelligence, providing the spatial grounding required for mobile robot navigation, human-robot interaction, and autonomous exploration. For robots operating in real indoor environments, a localization system should not only be accurate, but also be readily deployable in new scenes with minimal scene-specific preparation. Traditional indoor visual localization methods [ 20 , 2 , 27 , 35 ] typically rely on pre-built image databases or accurate 3D scene models. These representations are costly to construct, storage-intensive, and difficult to maintain, making them difficult to scale across many buildings and adapt to changing indoor environments.

paragraphs.en: Floorplans offer a lightweight and scalable map representation for indoor localization. Compared with image databases and 3D scene models, they are compact, widely available [ 13 , 32 ] , and relatively stable over time, making them attractive for localization systems deployed across many buildings. Ideally, a floorplan should serve as a directly queryable geometric map, allowing localization without constructing additional scene-specific databases. However, existing high-performing floorplan localization methods [ 5 , 12 , 45 ] still largely rely on a database-driven formulation: they discretize the SE ⁡ ( 2 ) \mathrm{SE}(2) pose space, precompute dense pose-indexed observations from the floorplan, and match query images against these entries for localization. In sequential settings, the same database-derived scores are further converted into observation likelihoods for histogram filtering, causing the database dependency to persist in temporal fusion. As a result, the limitation lies not merely in preprocessing cost, but in the discretized localization paradigm itself: once localization is tied to a finite pose-indexed database, localization precision, storage, and runtime all scale with the sampling resolution, creating an unfavorable trade-off among accuracy, efficiency, and scalability.
paragraphs.zh: 楼层平面图为室内定位提供了一种轻量且可扩展的地图表示方式。 与图像数据库和三维场景模型相比，楼层平面图体积小巧、广泛可用 [ 13 , 32 ]，并且随时间推移相对稳定，因此非常适合部署于多栋建筑中的定位系统。 理想情况下，楼层平面图应能作为可直接查询的几何地图使用，从而实现无需构建额外场景特定数据库的定位。 然而，现有高性能的楼层平面图定位方法 [ 5 , 12 , 45 ] 仍然主要依赖数据库驱动的方案：它们将 SE ⁡ ( 2 ) \mathrm{SE}(2) 位姿空间离散化，预先计算基于位姿索引的密集楼层平面图观测数据，并通过匹配查询图像与这些条目进行定位。 在序列场景中，这些源自数据库的评分还会被进一步转换为用于直方图滤波的观测似然值，导致数据库依赖关系在时间融合过程中依然存在。 因此，其局限性不仅在于预处理成本，更在于离散化的定位范式本身：一旦定位与有限的位姿索引数据库绑定，定位精度、存储需求和运行时间都将随采样分辨率的变化而调整，从而在准确性、效率和可扩展性之间形成不利的权衡。

paragraphs.en: This motivates a more practical and challenging setting: given only a floorplan, can we directly query it online to achieve accurate RGB-based single-frame and sequential localization in new environments, without constructing a scene-specific offline database?
paragraphs.zh: 这促使我们考虑一个更具实践意义但也更具挑战性的设定：在仅给定一张平面图的情况下，我们能否直接在线查询该图，从而在新环境中实现基于RGB的精确单帧定位和序列定位，而无需构建针对特定场景的离线数据库？

paragraphs.en: A useful clue comes from how humans localize themselves in unfamiliar indoor spaces. Rather than exhaustively comparing the current view with every possible location on the map, humans typically use the floorplan to narrow the search to a few plausible regions, and then refine their location by matching local geometric details with the current observation. However, realizing this coarse-to-fine intuition in an online localization system is non-trivial. First, the system must rapidly search the entire floorplan pose space online to identify plausible initial pose hypotheses. Second, these retrieved poses are inherently approximate: finite online sampling introduces discretization errors, while noisy and incomplete RGB-derived geometric observations further limit matching accuracy, making it challenging to recover accurate poses from such coarse hypotheses. Third, for sequential localization with histogram filtering, observation likelihoods over the discretized pose space are required to update the propagated motion prior, yet these likelihoods can no longer be densely evaluated from a precomputed scene-specific ray database.
paragraphs.zh: 一个有用的线索来自人类如何在陌生的室内空间中确定自身位置。 人类通常不会将当前视野与地图上所有可能的位置逐一比较，而是借助平面图将搜索范围缩小到几个合理区域，再通过匹配局部几何细节与当前观察结果来精确定位。 然而，要在这种在线定位系统中实现这种从粗略到精细的直觉并非易事。 首先，系统必须在线快速搜索整个平面图的姿态空间，以识别出合理的初始姿态假设。 其次，这些检索出的姿态本质上只是近似值：有限的在线采样会引入离散化误差，而带有噪声且不完整的 RGB 几何观察结果会进一步限制匹配精度，使得从如此粗略的假设中恢复精确姿态变得困难。 第三，对于采用直方图滤波的序列定位方法，需要在离散化的姿态空间上计算观察似然值，以便更新传播的运动先验；然而，这些似然值已无法通过预计算的场景特定射线数据库进行密集评估。

paragraphs.en: To address these challenges, we propose FreeLoc, an online RGB-based floorplan localization framework that treats the floorplan as a directly queryable geometric map rather than a scene-specific offline retrieval database, as shown in Fig. 1 . FreeLoc first retrieves a compact set of plausible pose anchors by querying geometric rays from the floorplan on the fly using a GPU-accelerated rotation-aware ray kernel. To refine these approximate anchors, we introduce a diffusion-aided pose refinement network that estimates residual pose corrections from the discrepancy between image-side and floorplan-side ray observations. Instead of relying on one-shot deterministic regression, we formulate pose refinement as an iterative denoising process, which better matches the nature of residual pose optimization and progressively corrects imperfect coarse anchors under ray-level geometric guidance. This allows FreeLoc to move beyond the resolution of coarse online samples and produce accurate pose hypotheses in continuous pose space without exhaustive dense sampling or precomputed scene-specific ray databases. To support sequential localization, we further integrate the online coarse-to-fine estimator into a probabilistic filtering pipeline. Rather than deriving dense observation likelihoods from an offline ray database, FreeLoc constructs observation likelihoods online from coarse-sampled candidates and refines their high-confidence regions using the refined pose hypotheses before Bayesian filtering [ 6 , 10 , 9 ] . This online likelihood construction bridges single-frame localization and temporal fusion without reintroducing a scene-specific database, enabling temporally consistent localization while preserving the immediate deployability of floorplans.
paragraphs.zh: 为应对这些挑战，我们提出了 FreeLoc——一种基于 RGB 的在线平面布局定位框架。该框架将平面布局视为可直接查询的几何地图，而非针对特定场景的离线检索数据库，如图 1 所示。 FreeLoc 首先通过 GPU 加速的旋转感知射线核，实时从平面布局中发射几何射线，检索出一组紧凑且可信的姿态锚点。 为了优化这些近似锚点，我们引入了一种扩散辅助的姿态优化网络，该网络根据图像侧与平面布局侧射线观测值之间的差异，估算出残差姿态修正量。 我们不依赖单次确定性回归，而是将姿态优化构造成一个迭代去噪过程。这一过程更贴合残差姿态优化的本质，并能在射线级几何引导下逐步修正不精确的粗略锚点。 这使得 FreeLoc 能够突破粗略在线样本的分辨率限制，在连续姿态空间中生成精确的姿态假设，而无需进行穷举式密集采样或使用预计算的场景特定射线数据库。 为支持序列定位，我们进一步将在线的粗到精估计器整合进一个概率过滤流程中。 FreeLoc 并未从离线射线数据库中推导密集的观测似然值，而是在线利用粗略采样的候选项构建观测似然值，并通过优化后的姿态假设对其高置信度区域进行修正，随后再进行贝叶斯过滤 [6, 10, 9]。 这种在线似然构建方法在单帧定位与时间融合之间架起了桥梁，既无需重新引入场景特定数据库，又能实现时间一致的定位，同时保留平面布局的即时部署能力。

paragraphs.en: Our contributions are summarized as follows. First, we propose FreeLoc, an online coarse-to-fine framework for RGB-based floorplan localization that eliminates scene-specific offline database construction and enables immediate deployment in new environments. Second, we introduce an efficient online geometric querying and diffusion-aided refinement scheme, which retrieves plausible pose anchors directly from the floorplan and progressively refines them into accurate continuous pose estimates. Third, we develop an online likelihood construction strategy that bridges single-frame localization and probabilistic temporal fusion, enabling histogram-filter-based sequential localization by constructing observation likelihoods from online sampled candidates and updating them with refined pose hypotheses. Finally, experiments on various datasets demonstrate that FreeLoc achieves SOTA accuracy and efficiency across representative localization methods from different paradigms, while real-world experiments further validate its practicality for indoor robotic localization.

paragraphs.en: Visual Localization. Visual localization is a fundamental problem in robotic perception and has been extensively studied for decades. Early methods commonly formulate it as image retrieval [ 20 , 2 , 1 , 8 , 22 ] , where a query image is matched to a pre-built reference database to infer its pose. With advances in 3D vision, correspondence-based approaches [ 27 , 35 , 24 , 26 ] construct 3D scene models, typically via structure-from-motion (SfM) [ 33 ] , and estimate the 6-DoF camera pose from 2D-3D matches. Beyond ground-level reference maps, cross-view localization has also explored globally available satellite imagery as a spatial reference for ground-level localization [ 14 ] . More recently, neural scene representations such as NeRF [ 30 ] and 3DGS [ 23 ] have also been explored for pose estimation by relating query images to scene-specific representations [ 50 , 48 , 18 ] . However, these approaches depend on pre-constructed databases or scene-specific representations, leading to high storage costs and limited generalization to unseen environments.
paragraphs.zh: 视觉定位。 视觉定位是机器人感知领域的一个基本问题，几十年来一直受到广泛研究。 早期方法通常将其表述为图像检索问题 [ 20 , 2 , 1 , 8 , 22 ]，即将查询图像与预建的参考数据库进行匹配，以推断其位姿。 随着三维视觉技术的进步，基于对应关系的方法 [ 27 , 35 , 24 , 26 ] 开始构建三维场景模型，通常通过运动恢复结构（SfM）[ 33 ] 实现，并基于二维与三维特征点的匹配来估计相机的 6-DoF 位姿。 除了地面参考地图外，跨视角定位还探索了全球可用的卫星图像，将其作为地面定位的空间参考 [ 14 ]。 近期，NeRF [ 30 ] 和 3DGS [ 23 ] 等神经场景表示方法也被用于位姿估计，通过将查询图像与场景特定的表示相关联来实现 [ 50 , 48 , 18 ]。 然而，这些方法依赖于预先构建的数据库或场景特定的表示，导致存储成本高昂，并且难以泛化到未见过的环境中。

paragraphs.en: Floorplan Localization. Floorplan localization estimates camera pose with respect to a given floorplan, offering a lightweight alternative to image databases and full 3D reconstructions. Early methods [ 4 , 42 , 11 , 46 ] rely on LiDAR scans matched against floorplan geometry, while later approaches [ 19 , 7 , 43 , 44 ] use depth cameras or visual odometry to obtain geometric observations. Although effective, these methods require dedicated sensors or assumptions such as known room or camera height, limiting practical applicability. To improve accessibility, recent works have explored RGB-only floorplan localization. LaLaLoc [ 17 ] and LaLaLoc++ [ 16 ] embed panoramic observations and floorplan-derived layouts into a shared latent space for retrieval. PF-Net [ 21 ] formulates localization as differentiable particle filtering, and LASER [ 31 ] aligns image features with rotation-aware circular map features rendered from rasterized floorplan geometry. However, many of these methods assume upright camera poses, making them less suitable for handheld or head-mounted settings. Another line of work [ 12 , 31 , 29 , 52 ] incorporates semantic cues, but semantic annotations are often unavailable in standard floorplans. F 3 Loc [ 5 ] and UnLoc [ 45 ] take an important step toward practical RGB-based floorplan localization by using geometry-only floorplans and images captured under arbitrary camera poses. They predict floorplan depth from gravity-aligned images and localize the camera by matching the resulting rays against a dense pre-sampled floorplan-ray database. However, constructing such a database requires time-consuming scene-specific preprocessing and creates an inherent trade-off among localization accuracy, sampling density, and storage cost, limiting flexibility in new environments. In contrast, our method performs online localization without scene-specific offline ray databases, enabling efficient and accurate deployment in new scenes using only the provided geometric floorplan.

paragraphs.en: Since RGB images in practical scenarios may be captured by handheld or head-mounted devices with arbitrary roll and pitch, we first normalize each image into a gravity-aligned view. Given the camera intrinsic matrix 𝐊 \mathbf{K} and the image roll r r and pitch p p , the rotation from the camera frame to the gravity-aligned frame is defined as 𝐑 g ​ c = ( 𝐑 z ​ ( r ) ​ 𝐑 x ​ ( p ) ) ⊤ \mathbf{R}_{gc}=(\mathbf{R}_{z}(r)\mathbf{R}_{x}(p))^{\top} . The roll and pitch can be obtained from inertial sensors available on modern mobile devices, or estimated by off-the-shelf single-image calibration methods such as GeoCalib [ 40 ] when sensor readings are unavailable. paragraphs.en: Baseline and Metrics. We compare our method with representative floorplan localization approaches from different categories. F 3 Loc [ 5 ] is used as the primary baseline, as it is a strong state-of-the-art depth-based method, and we adopt its monocular version for comparison. We also evaluate against PF-Net [ 21 ] and LASER [ 31 ] , two representative non-depth-based methods for differentiable particle-filter-based and feature-based floorplan localization, respectively. Following prior work [ 5 , 31 ] , for single-frame localization, we report recall at translation thresholds of 0.1 0.1 m, 0.5 0.5 m, and 1.0 1.0 m, together with recall under the joint pose threshold of 1.0 1.0 m and 30 ∘ 30^{\circ} . For sequential localization, we report success rate and tracking accuracy. A trajectory is considered successful at threshold X X m if the predictions stay within X X m of the ground truth over the last 10 frames. We also report RMSE over the last 10 frames for both successful and all trajectories. Following F3Loc, our default sequential evaluation uses GT-derived inter-frame ego-motion for controlled comparison; robustness to noisy and temporarily unavailable ego-motion is evaluated in Sec. 4.5.

paragraphs.en: Results on Gibson(f) and Structured3D. As shown in Table 1 , our FreeLoc consistently outperforms all baselines on both Gibson(f) and Structured3D. Compared with the strongest baseline F 3 Loc, ours improves all recall metrics by 4.7 4.7 – 8.7 8.7 percentage points on Gibson(f) and 1.4 1.4 – 8.9 8.9 percentage points on Structured3D, demonstrating consistent gains across different data distributions. We attribute these improvements mainly to the proposed pose refinement stage. Unlike offline database matching, whose accuracy is constrained by the discretization of pre-sampled floorplan poses, our refinement module optimizes coarse anchors in a continuous pose space, allowing predictions to move beyond sampled locations and achieve finer pose accuracy. Moreover, while both F 3 Loc and our method benefit from floorplan-ray representations and substantially outperform PF-Net and LASER, FreeLoc further improves upon F 3 Loc by replacing dense offline ray matching with online coarse sampling and continuous pose refinement.

paragraphs.en: Results on Gibson(t). Table 2 reports the sequential localization results on Gibson(t), where the sequence length is set to 100 frames. Our method achieves the best success rate and overall tracking accuracy. Compared with F 3 Loc, FreeLoc improves the success rate by 13.5 13.5 percentage points and reduces RMSE all by 82.8 % 82.8\% , demonstrating substantially more robust tracking over long trajectories. For RMSE succ , FreeLoc remains comparable to F 3 Loc, with only a marginal difference ( 0.15 ​ m 0.15\,\mathrm{m} vs. 0.14 ​ m 0.14\,\mathrm{m} ), indicating that both methods achieve similarly low errors once successfully localized. This slight gap mainly stems from reconstructing dense observation likelihoods from sparse online candidates, which may slightly reduce local precision compared with dense likelihood evaluation over a precomputed ray database. Nevertheless, by initializing observation likelihoods from online sampled candidates and updating them with refined pose hypotheses, FreeLoc provides reliable frame-level evidence for histogram filtering, enabling stable sequential localization without an offline ray database. Detailed qualitative comparisons are provided in Appendix B.3 .

paragraphs.en: Timing. We report the average per-frame inference time under the Gibson(t) sequential localization setting, together with the scene-specific offline sampling cost required by database-based methods. The offline sampling time is measured on the first Gibson(t) test scene, which covers approximately 10 ​ m × 6 ​ m 10\,\mathrm{m}\times 6\,\mathrm{m} . Following the official F 3 Loc implementation, we use its released sampling code and testing-time sampling resolution to construct the offline ray database. F 3 Loc achieves fast inference ( 0.014 ​ s 0.014\,\mathrm{s} per frame) once the scene-specific ray database has been precomputed, but constructing this database takes 1.48 1.48 hours for a single scene. In contrast, our method localizes directly from the provided floorplan without offline ray-database construction, while still running about 15 15 Hz ( 0.069 ​ s 0.069\,\mathrm{s} per frame) including online sampling. Therefore, when deployed in a new scene from scratch, our unified coarse-to-fine framework substantially reduces the overall localization cost by eliminating the time-consuming scene-specific preprocessing stage.

paragraphs.en: To further validate real-world deployability, we build a real-world setting from the HGE building in the LaMAR dataset [ 36 ] , since no public real-world indoor dataset provides both continuous RGB sequences and corresponding floorplan maps under our target setting. HGE is a large-scale indoor scene with rooms, corridors, and open halls, covering about 130 ​ m × 130 ​ m 130\,\mathrm{m}\times 130\,\mathrm{m} . The sequences are captured by a handheld iPhone with a narrow 48 ∘ 48^{\circ} FoV. As shown in Fig. 3 , the posterior distribution is initially multi-modal due to the large search space and the ambiguity of narrow-FoV observations. After convergence, the estimated trajectory remains closely aligned with the ground truth throughout the sequence, demonstrating the stable long-term localization capability of FreeLoc in a large and structurally complex real-world environment. paragraphs.en: Coarse-to-Fine Localization Analysis. We analyze the behavior of Diffusion-Aided Pose Refinement under different qualities of coarse initialization. As shown in Table 3 , when coarse hypotheses lie within 0.5 ​ m 0.5\,\mathrm{m} , 1.0 ​ m 1.0\,\mathrm{m} , and 1.5 ​ m 1.5\,\mathrm{m} of the ground truth, diffusion refinement consistently reduces the average translation error, demonstrating effective residual pose correction from plausible initializations. In contrast, when all coarse hypotheses are considered regardless of their initialization quality, the improvement is marginal ( 3.14 ​ m 3.14\,\mathrm{m} to 3.09 ​ m 3.09\,\mathrm{m} ). This limited gain arises mainly because the “All” set contains many poorly initialized hypotheses, including cross-room cases that are geometrically far from the ground-truth pose. Such hypotheses fall outside the effective range of local residual correction and are therefore difficult to recover through refinement alone. These results clarify the intended division of labor in our coarse-to-fine framework: Online Coarse Pose Retrieval narrows the global search to geometrically plausible pose hypotheses, while Diffusion-Aided Pose Refinement performs precise local residual correction to further improve localization accuracy.

paragraphs.en: We presented FreeLoc, an online RGB-based floorplan localization framework that treats the floorplan as a directly queryable geometric map rather than a dense scene-specific offline database. FreeLoc builds a unified online coarse-to-fine pipeline that combines on-the-fly floorplan ray querying with diffusion-aided pose refinement to retrieve plausible anchors and refine them into accurate continuous pose estimates. The same coarse anchors and refined hypotheses are further used to construct online observation likelihoods for sequential localization, bridging single-frame localization and probabilistic temporal fusion without offline databases. Experiments on various datasets demonstrate accurate and efficient localization, as well as immediate deployability in new environments.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 FreeLoc，这是一个基于 RGB 的在线平面布局定位框架，它将平面布局视为可直接查询的几何地图，而非针对特定场景的密集离线数据库。 FreeLoc 构建了一个统一的在线由粗到精处理流程，将实时平面布局射线查询与扩散辅助姿态优化相结合，以获取可信的锚点，并将其优化为精确的连续姿态估计值。 相同的粗略锚点和优化后的假设进一步用于构建在线观测似然度，以实现序列定位，从而在没有离线数据库的情况下连接单帧定位与概率性时间融合。 在多个数据集上进行的实验表明，FreeLoc 能够实现准确高效的定位，并可在新环境中立即部署。

paragraphs.en: Although our method demonstrates strong localization performance and favorable deployability, its generalization remains limited under substantially different camera settings or scene distributions. This limitation mainly stems from the monocular floorplan-depth estimator, which is sensitive to camera intrinsics, field of view, and scene scale. Moreover, while FreeLoc supports efficient inference in typical indoor environments, the enlarged search space of very large floorplans can still affect real-time performance, although FreeLoc retains faster and more convenient deployment than existing database-based approaches. Future work will explore more generalizable depth estimation and hierarchical floorplan querying to improve both cross-domain robustness and runtime scalability.

paragraphs.en: This soft correspondence preserves the ray-wise structure while relaxing strict index-wise matching. paragraphs.en: We obtain the complete HGE building floorplan from the official source and use it as the localization map. To align the original LaMAR annotations with our floorplan localization setting, we convert the provided SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) poses from the global world coordinate system into SE ⁡ ( 2 ) \mathrm{SE}(2) poses in the floorplan coordinate system. Specifically, we manually select four salient landmarks that can be reliably identified in both the RGB observations and the floorplan. For each landmark, we record its 2D position in the LaMAR world coordinate system and its corresponding pixel coordinate on the floorplan. These four point correspondences provide eight constraints, which are sufficient to estimate the six parameters of a 2D affine transformation in a least-squares [ 3 ] manner. We then apply the estimated affine transformation to all ground-truth trajectory positions. For orientation, we extract the yaw heading from the original quaternion and transform it consistently into the floorplan coordinate system using the linear part of the estimated affine transformation. This yields the final SE ⁡ ( 2 ) \mathrm{SE}(2) pose annotations on the floorplan.
paragraphs.zh: 我们从官方来源获取完整的 HGE 建筑平面图，并将其用作定位地图。 为了使原始的 LaMAR 标注与我们的平面图定位设置对齐，我们将提供的 SE(3) 位姿从全局世界坐标系转换为平面图坐标系中的 SE(2) 位姿。 具体来说，我们手动选择了四个显著的地标，这些地标在 RGB 观测图像和平面图中都能被可靠地识别出来。 对于每个地标，我们记录其在 LaMAR 世界坐标系中的二维位置以及其在平面图上的对应像素坐标。 这四组点对应关系提供了八个约束条件，足以通过最小二乘 [3] 方法估计出二维仿射变换的六个参数。 接着，我们将估计出的仿射变换应用于所有真实轨迹位置。 关于方向，我们从原始四元数中提取偏航角，并使用估计出的仿射变换的线性部分将其一致地转换到平面图坐标系中。 这样便得到了平面图上的最终 SE(2) 位姿标注。

paragraphs.en: To better match the floorplan geometry to the visual observations, we manually remove non-geometric annotations such as room numbers and stair labels. We also remove doors at traversable connections along the collected trajectories while preserving other doors as solid walls, since they are mostly closed during LaMAR data collection. Landmark selection, floorplan alignment, and preprocessing use no validation or test trajectories and are performed solely to adapt LaMAR to the floorplan-localization setting, rather than to tune the localization method. paragraphs.en: Table 6 presents the quantitative results on the real-world HGE building dataset. The HGE building is a challenging floorplan localization setting, covering a large spatial extent of approximately 130 ​ m × 130 ​ m 130\,\mathrm{m}\times 130\,\mathrm{m} with complex indoor layouts and repetitive structural patterns. Despite this difficulty, depth-based methods can still produce relatively concentrated single-frame likelihoods in regions with moderate ray depths and sufficient geometric constraints. These likelihoods provide useful frame-level evidence for temporal filtering, enabling sequential localization to reach a reliable level of accuracy over time.

paragraphs.en: We first compare our diffusion-aided pose refinement with ICP optimization in the main paper. Since residual pose refinement can naturally be formulated as a geometric registration problem, ICP serves as a representative deterministic alternative. However, ICP relies on reliable geometric correspondences and local alignment, whereas our ray observations are sparse and imperfect due to coarse pose errors and image-side ray prediction noise, limiting the effectiveness of deterministic alignment. This comparison demonstrates the benefit of learned refinement over conventional geometric optimization, but does not isolate whether the gain originates from the learned ray-discrepancy representation or the diffusion formulation itself. We therefore further introduce a simpler learned direct-regression baseline to specifically examine the contribution of diffusion-based refinement.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在主论文中首先将我们的扩散辅助姿态精修方法与 ICP 优化进行了比较。 由于残差姿态精修天然可以表述为一个几何配准问题，因此 ICP 可作为一种具有代表性的确定性替代方案。 然而，ICP 依赖于可靠的几何对应关系和局部对齐，而我们的射线观测由于粗略的姿态误差和图像侧射线预测噪声而稀疏且不完整，这限制了确定性对齐的有效性。 这一比较展示了学习式精修相较于传统几何优化的优势，但并未明确区分这种增益究竟源于学习的射线差异表示，还是扩散公式本身。 因此，我们进一步引入一个更简单的学习式直接回归基线，以专门考察基于扩散的精修方法所做出的贡献。

paragraphs.en: As shown in Table 7 , diffusion-aided refinement consistently outperforms direct regression across all reported metrics, including a 2.8 2.8 percentage-point gain in SR@0.2m and a 25 % 25\% reduction in RMSE all . paragraphs.en: Compared with one-shot regression, iterative denoising is better suited to residual pose optimization by progressively refining pose corrections toward geometrically consistent solutions. Moreover, noisy and locally ambiguous ray-level discrepancies make a single deterministic prediction less flexible in capturing uncertainty in the residual correction. paragraphs.en: We further compare with UnLoc [ 45 ] , which extends F 3 Loc with stronger foundation-model-based monocular depth estimation using Depth Anything V2 [ 47 ] .
